input: Advice needed for family investment decision: 2nd hand condo or ETF? Hi Everyone, appreciate your advices here as I've been struggling with this complex decision. Facts first: \-We are 1st generation immigrants, a nuclear family of 3 (one preschool-age boy and there won't be more kids); \-We stay in a resale HDB (4 rooms) in the RCR area. We bought this HDB years ago and we still like it for its very reasonable and spacious layout, which we don't see in most new HDBs and condos; \-Both me and my husband work in private companies that don't have much job security, our combined monthly income is circa. 20Ksgd; \-We are not susceptible to consumerism and we don't have extravagant hobbies (just reading and general sports mostly), the only expensive annual cash outflow is on a mid-distance overseas travelling; \-By the time our kid is going to the primary school, we wish we could stay just next to the school (5min walk at most) so that everyone in the family can get more sleep; \-Last but not least, this is probably not a fact yet (I certainly do hope so), but our boy is likely an inattentive ADHD. We have not have him diagnosed, but from the feedback we got from the preschool teachers and from our own observation, this is 80% true. Hence, we do not count on him to become successful academically and financially. We are content enough that he could develop into a upright and happy adult. Alrightie, thanks for reaching thus far. Now our problems/struggles: \-The only good school within 1km of our HDB is still a bit far away, meaning we need to take a bus there in the morning. Also for various reasons, I don't see my boy fit into that school. So if we are to change school, we might need to rent for the next 15 years (as we want to stay just next door to the primary school, secondary school and etc.) \-Given my kid's condition, our family investment strategy is that we prefer to invest wisely over the next two decades, save enough money for my kid's college (if he is able to attend one) and for him to find his lifelong passion (the only way out for an ADHD), and for us to retire comfortably. We are debating between two options: \-one is to sell our HDB, combined with our cash reserve, we could afford about 50% of a two-room resale condo. In this case, the effective annual return from this condo is about 2-3%, but our cashflows will be very limited as we need to bear the 50% mortgage. Since we don't feel quite secure about our incomes, we are hesitant on this. Also, since we are most likely to rent homes near school, this condo might be rented out anyway and will not become a "home" for us effectively. \-the other option is to continue living in our HDB, rent it out after my kid goes to the primary school and continue to rent until he goes to college. My secret fear for this option is that since it's a liquid investment, my husband (who spend his spare time studying the stock market), might not be able to resist his urge to trade. input: What should be done about Singapore’s HDB system? We’ve all heard by now CSJ’s famous rants against the ruling party and the HDB Leasehold system.
